instruction:
Fix `packages/catalog-model/src/entity/formerNames.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Security review M1 and L3, accepted at Gate 3. M1: parseEntityFormerRefs has no cap on entries and does not deduplicate problems, so a small annotation can inflate the stitched entity to megabytes and fill the claim table. Do all of this, keeping the module-private constant style, with no new export: (1) add `const MAX_FORMER_NAMES = 100;` and read only the first 100 comma-separated parts; when there are more, add one problem with entry `<n> more entries` (n is the number ignored) and reason `only the first 100 entries are read`; (2) report at most one problem for empty entries, however many there are; (3) report each distinct entry and reason pair once; (4) add `const MAX_ECHOED_ENTRY_LENGTH = 64;` and shorten the `entry` of every problem to its first 64 characters plus `...` when longer. L3: control characters are accepted. Add `const CONTROL_CHARACTER_PATTERN = /\p{Cc}/u;` (a Unicode property keeps eslint no-control-regex quiet) and check it right after the empty check, rejecting such an entry with reason `it holds a control character`, before any parsing. In every problem's `entry`, replace each control character with `?`, so none reaches a status item or the database. Add a sentence on the 100-entry limit to the TSDoc of parseEntityFormerRefs. The return shape and every other rule stay as they are.

Fix `plugins/catalog-backend/src/service/createRouter.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Security review L1, accepted at Gate 3, in the GET /entities/by-former-name/:kind/:namespace/:name handler. `await auditorEvent?.success()` runs before the not-found check, so a 404 logs initiated, succeeded and failed, and a success omits the resolved ref. Move the success call to after the `if (!currentRef)` check, so a miss logs only initiated and failed, and pass the resolved ref: `await auditorEvent?.success({ meta: { currentEntityRef: currentRef } });`. The person chose this at Gate 3, and it replaces the plan's 'no target in its meta'. Change nothing else, and leave the by-name route as it is.

Fix `docs/features/software-catalog/api.md` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Security review L2, accepted at Gate 3: the sentence `These cases cannot be told apart.` in the `GET /entities/by-former-name` section is false, since the live-entity and contested checks ignore what the caller may read. Replace that sentence with text saying: the 404 response itself is the same in all these cases, but it is not a guarantee that a hidden entity stays hidden. Someone who can read an entity that claims a name, or who can register an entity that claims it, can tell from a 200 or a 404 whether an entity they cannot read sits at that name. The warning on a claimant of a contested name also shows that another entity claims it, even one that the reader cannot see. Keep it to a short paragraph. Follow docs/contribute/doc-style-guide.md and keep prose wrapped as the file does.
